posts.title: A Human Soul Inside a Bear & a Tray
posts.description: An Early Intimation of Death and the Inanimate I have written before on the topic that I call an early intimation of death and the inanimate which involved and IKEA panda bear. The link is above. But of late as I look around my house and gaze on all the memorabilia from my family and of my life with Rosemary for 52 years I am overwhelmed. I cannot see myself throwing any into the garbage or taking some of it to dollar stores. It has to do with my renewed awareness of what New York Time On Language columnist William Safire called resistentialism. He defined it as inanimate objects making humans aware that they also had free will. Any photographer who may own a digital camera will know how that manifests itself. These cameras will randomly do what they (I almost believe in using that pronoun) want. posts.title: Impossible to Forget
posts.description: It is not often that I remember a precise date in my mind. There is one that I do remember. When I was born in Buenos Aires on August 31, 1942 my birth was recorded by a photographer with a magnesium flash. That burst of light is when I decided that someday I would become a photographer. There is another date that I can never forget. On 26 January 1981 I was shooting stills in Studio 41of the CBC in Vancouver. I had been hired to take photographs of the Paul Anka Show. A good looking young man showed up. That day was his 21 st birthday and he had made a huge million dollar contract with his hockey team owners. Wayne Gretzky posed for me and he had a lovely “aw shuks” attitude. Such was my excitement that I did not notice that my back light stand was showing between his legs. Two years later I was in Edmonton assigned to photograph the Canuck’s head coach Bill LaForge whose team was plastered by Gretzky's Oilers the evening that I was there. posts.title: A Leaf in Time
posts.description: 25 November 2026 In these last few years I have been obsessively interested in finding the etymology of words and expressions in the two languages that I speak, Spanish and English. It was not too long ago that I thought hard of the word routine and rutina in Spanish and suddenly figured that it came from taking the same path over and over. Look up the origin of “ waiting for the shoe to drop” and you will get what I mean. It is in this century that we have finally (is this good?) not needed to go to the library to check on facts or consult the Encyclopaedia (note that wicked a) Britannica that might be full of dust in the attic. My life without my Rosemary is now almost pure routine. My female cat Niña expects to be fed in the morning, at noon, late in the afternoon and now that it gets darker earlier she stares at me at 7, if I am on my bed, as she wants her treats.
